record.original_question: If X subseteq Σ+ satisfies p(x) < p(w) for all x in X, must w have at most |X|+1-r(X) disjoint X-factorizations?

evidence.quote: Denote by p(w) the smallest period of an wordwin Σ+. Let Xsubseteq Σ+ satisfying p(x) < p(w) for all xin X. Is it true that w has at most |X| + 1- r(X) disjoint X-factorizations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $\Sigma^+$ the set of nonempty finite words over $\Sigma$. For a word $w\in\Sigma^+$, let $p(w)$ denote the smallest period of $w$, i.e., the least positive integer $p$ such that $w[i]=w[i+p]$ for all valid $i$. For a finite set $X\subseteq\Sigma^+$, an $X$-factorization of $w$ is a tuple $(x_1,\ldots,x_k)$ with each $x_i\in X$ and $w=x_1x_2\cdots x_k$. Two $X$-factorizations $(x_1,\ldots,x_k)$ and $(y_1,\ldots,y_\ell)$ of $w$ are called disjoint if the sets of cut positions $\{|x_1\cdots x_i|:1\le i<k\}$ and $\{|y_1\cdots y_j|:1\le j<\ell\}$ are disjoint. Let $r(X)$ denote the combinatorial rank of $X$ (the smallest cardinality of a set $Y\subseteq\Sigma^+$ such that $X\subseteq Y^+$).

Question: Suppose $X\subseteq\Sigma^+$ is finite and satisfies $p(x)<p(w)$ for every $x\in X$. Must $w$ admit at most $|X|+1-r(X)$ pairwise disjoint $X$-factorizations?
